# Honest Code: Stop Fighting the Machine

> A software architecture book by Adam Zachary Wasserman. Thirteen chapters, eleven languages, with instrumented nanosecond execution traces published for independent verification.

## What it is

*Honest Code: Stop Fighting the Machine* is a software architecture book by Adam Zachary Wasserman. Its argument is that most complexity in production code comes from hiding state inside classes and objects, and that every mainstream language already provides the alternative: pure functions, flat data, and composition.

The book sets out sixteen principles, numbered P01 through P16, for code where state is visible, functions are pure, and input and output happen only at the boundaries of the system.

## Structure and evidence

- **Thirteen chapters.** All thirteen are free to read in full at <https://honestcode.software/chapters/>.
- **Eleven languages**, each shown as a side-by-side comparison of a dishonest pattern against its honest equivalent: C#, C++, Dart, Go, Java, Kotlin, PHP, Python, Ruby, Swift, TypeScript.
- **Measured, not asserted.** Every nanosecond figure on the site comes from instrumented harnesses run on real hardware. The source, the Dockerfile, and the raw results are published at <https://github.com/adamzwasserman/honest-code-traces> so any third party can re-run them. The analysis is at <https://honestcode.software/evidence.html>.

## The sixteen principles

P01 dict-lookup dispatch over conditional chains. P02 TypedDict over classes. P03 pure functions over methods. P04 input and output at the boundary. P05 flat composition over inheritance. P06 DOM as state. P07 HTML attributes over imperative JavaScript. P08 typed exceptions at the boundary. P09 SQL over application caches. P10 pure assertions over mocks. P11 type declarations. P12 context managers. P13 configuration as parameters. P14 simple Gherkin as a proxy for honest architecture. P15 declarative over lifecycle hooks. P16 the strangler pattern.

## Positions the book argues

- The enemy of early type checking is classes, not dynamic typing.
- Pure boolean predicates over strings constitute a near-free type system.
- The reference architecture is FastAPI with HTMX and no client-side framework.
- Shared mutable state is the root cause of most bugs that reach production.

## How it relates to the rest of the work

Honest Code is the practitioner-facing statement of principles that the Open Honest Foundation turns into standards and measurement instruments. The Honest Framework is the correct-by-construction implementation of those principles; the Slop Audit is the instrument that measures adherence to them. DATAOS, the DOM-as-state architecture used in principle P06, is documented separately at <https://dataos.software> and implemented in multicardz.

- Open Honest Foundation: <https://openhonest.org>
- DATAOS: <https://dataos.software>
- multicardz, the production application built on these principles: <https://multicardz.com>

## Author

Adam Zachary Wasserman, author and independent researcher. Forty years in enterprise software, including CTO at IATA and Director of Consulting at CGI.
